w: Tucked inside Belgrade Fortress next to the spring of Saint Petka, this small church has been rebuilt more than once — founded in the early fifteenth century, remodelled in 1869, and fully reconstructed in 1925. Crowds still gather every year for Saint Petka's feast day, drawn to one of the best loved churches in the city.
s: A fortress church rebuilt three times over
_facts: Located in Belgrade Fortress; original church built in the early 15th century
Dedicated to the Nativity of Mary
Near the spring of Saint Petka; draws large crowds on her feast day

w: A royal garden once stood here, succeeded by what became one of central Belgrade's best-loved parks and a protected botanical monument. It was open to the public from 1944 until 2025, when police fenced it off; since March that year it has served as a camp for pro-government demonstrators opposing anti-corruption protests, leaving the grounds damaged.
s: A royal garden turned protest-camp flashpoint
_facts: Developed from a royal garden, itself successor to an older garden
Open to the public from 1944 until 2025
Since 6 March 2025 fenced off and used as a camp for pro-government protesters opposing anti-corruption demonstrations

w: Serbia's only theatre dedicated entirely to musicals sits on Terazije square, staging home-grown versions of Chicago, Kiss Me Kate and more. A top-to-bottom renovation between 2003 and 2005 left it one of the most technologically advanced theatres in the country, still going strong on Belgrade's grandest boulevard.
_facts: Only theatre in Serbia exclusively producing musicals
Has staged Serbian versions of Chicago, Kiss Me Kate and others
Renovated 2003-2005 into one of the most technologically advanced theatres in Serbia

w: The story goes that founder Persida Milenković dreamed three times that a monastery should rise on this spot in Senjak — and in 1936 it did, consecrated as an outpost of the Kuveždin Monastery. Its nuns once embroidered vestments and curtains for the Patriarchal chapel, and four Serbian archbishops now lie buried within its walls.
s: A monastery built after a founder's dream
_facts: Foundations consecrated August 1935; built and consecrated October 1936 as metochion of Kuveždin Monastery
Legend holds founder Persida Milenković dreamed three times the monastery should be built there
Nuns made embroidered vestments and curtains for the Patriarchal chapel
Four Serbian archbishops are buried within the monastery
